summary: This lecture from Shaykh Ali Mashhour's ongoing series on Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah focuses on night prayer (Salat al-Layl) and witr salah. The speaker explains that witr, meaning an odd number, is minimally one rakah but can be performed as three, five, seven, or nine rakahs with specific tashahhud patterns. He emphasizes that the Prophet encouraged witr as the final prayer of the night, clarifies misconceptions about the Sunnah of Fajr, and addresses prohibited times for optional prayer—after Fajr until sunrise, around noon, and after Asr until sunset. These prohibitions exist because pagan cultures historically worshipped celestial bodies during sunrise and sunset, times when Iblis is most influential in leading people astray.
